sources.title: Integrating Planning and Learning: The PRODIGY Architecture
sources.access: Public author-hosted PDF; title page, printed pp.24 and 26 visually checked; selected sections 2, 4.1–4.4 read; no redistribution license inferred

implemented: Planner integrated with rule acquisition modules QUALITY and HAMLET; Table 12 reports bounded logistics tests.
learned: Control rules from planning traces; HAMLET generates and refines rules using examples, QUALITY can use an expert-provided alternative or further search.
designed: Planner, domain operators, goals, quality criteria, search and learning algorithms.
limit: Runtime reduction reported as not significant for HAMLET; rule matching utility cost remains unresolved. Training uses supplied domains and task metrics. No evolved learning mechanism or reproductive heredity.
ora: Useful information should improve net outcomes after its own computation and storage costs, not merely task score.

sources.access: Publisher abstract only; full methods not reviewed

implemented: Reactive planning with belief, desire and intention representations; author reports robot navigation and emergency-task tests.
learned: Current observations and inferred beliefs may be acquired; independent learning of procedure specifications not established.

sources.title: R-CAST: Integrating Team Intelligence for Human-Centered Teamwork
sources.access: Public proceedings PDF; pp.1540–1541 images checked; copyright AAAI

implemented: Human-agent teamwork with shared process representations and context-sensitive decision aids; selected simulated evaluation with 30 participants.
learned: Context updates and adaptive decision support reported; acquisition of new collaboration rules not established by selected material.
designed: Team process, context representation, decision framework and task cues.
limit: Human-agent versus human-only teams differ in composition, so aggregate performance does not isolate one cognitive module; simulation and author reports are not field validation.
ora: Group-level benefit does not prove an individual developed cognition; isolate source of coordination and contribution of each actor.
